name: CR-Int-17-misc-16
generalfeedback: We want to solve \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] using the substitution \({{CT:3}} = 2\sin(z)\). So, if \({{CT:3}} = 2\sin(z)\) then \(d{{CT:3}} = 2\cos(z)dz\) and \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int{{CT:2}}d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int \frac{1}{[4-(2\sin(z))^2]^{3/2}}2\cos(z)dz \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int \frac{2\cos(z)dz}{[4-4\sin^2(z)]^{3/2}} \\&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int \frac{2\cos(z)dz}{[4(1-\sin^2(z))]^{3/2}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int \frac{2\cos(z)dz}{4^{3/2}[1-\sin^2(z)]^{3/2}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int \frac{\cos(z)dz}{4[\cos^2(z)]^{3/2}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int \frac{\cos(z)dz}{4\cos^3(z)} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \int \frac{dz}{4\cos^2(z)} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{1}{4}\int \sec^2(z)dz \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{\tan(z)}{4} +c \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{1}{4}\tan\left[\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)\right]+c \end{array}\] We need \[\int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] so, recall that if \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)+c\] then \[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\] Thus, define \[F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:4}}\] Then, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}} - {{CT:6}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}} \end{array}\]
